subject: Gross margin model update w/ meter v2 assumptions (need Product confirmation)
body:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 20, 2026 at 9:14 AM PT
Subject: Gross margin model update w/ meter v2 assumptions (need Product confirmation)
Attachments: GM_Model_v2026.02_MeterV2_Assumptions.xlsx; MeterV2_vs_V1_DeltaNotes_2026-02-20.pdf

Evelyn / Nikhil —

FP&A updated the gross margin model to reflect the meter v2 changes coming out of the metering hardening work (billed_tokens field, retry/dedupe fixes, embeddings batch accounting, cache-hit attribution, and Dedicated GPU-seconds v2 definitions).

Before we lock this into the month-end / Q1 forecast decks, can you confirm the *expected behavioral changes* on the Product side (i.e., what will/should change for customers vs what is purely measurement)?

Summary of what’s updated in the model (high-level):
1) Hosted API (tokens/requests)
- We move from “raw tokens observed in request logs” to “billed_tokens” as the revenue meter.
- Assumption: billed_tokens should be ~flat to down vs current ledger in cases where we were double-counting server retries/fallback (streaming + retry paths).
- Assumption: cache-hit attribution will shift cost allocation (and some internal margin reporting) but not increase customer billed tokens.

2) Embeddings (batched inputs)
- Assumption: fixed bug where we were overstating billed units on multi-input requests (counting per-request overhead more than once). This reduces billed units for high-batch customers.

3) Dedicated (GPU-seconds v2)
- Assumption: clarified idle + autoscaling transition accounting; net effect is small, but we should expect some accounts to see lower reported usage when pools are scaling down.

Key assumptions in the spreadsheet (tabs: “Hosted_API_Assumptions”, “Embeddings_Assumptions”, “Dedicated_Assumptions”):
- Retry double-count rate pre-fix: 0.3%–0.8% of requests (weighted by streaming usage); post-fix: ~0.05% (residual client retries that are correctly billed once).
- Cache-hit rate: 6% baseline (self-serve), 11% enterprise (heavier repeated prefixes); used for cost allocation and COGS per billed token.
- Meter freshness / late events: assume 99.5% of usage events land within 24h; remaining caught in T+3 backfill (but revenue recognized in period based on freeze window).

What I need from Product (please reply inline):
A) Do we expect any *customer behavior* changes as a result of the meter v2 rollout? (e.g., changes in retry patterns once they see billed vs raw tokens; changes in batching behavior; changes in caching usage patterns)
B) For pricing experiment analysis: can we treat meter v2 as “measurement correction only,” or do we expect any downstream changes (e.g., due to new SDK fields / documentation updates) that could shift usage?
C) Any planned changes to free tier/overage copy, quotas, or plan limits that could change demand in late Feb / March? (We need to separate those from metering impacts.)

If you can confirm by EOD Monday, we can keep the forecast cadence.

Thanks,
Rishi
—
Rishi Malhotra
FP&A Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 20, 2026 at 11:02 AM PT
Subject: Re: Gross margin model update w/ meter v2 assumptions (need Product confirmation)

Rishi — replying inline.

> A) Do we expect any customer behavior changes as a result of the meter v2 rollout?

Expected: minimal. The intent is a measurement correction + clearer surfaces.
- Retry/dedupe fixes: customers shouldn’t need to change anything. If anything, we may see *slightly fewer* “defensive retries” from customers who previously suspected over-billing, but I wouldn’t model that as a near-term usage increase.
- Billed vs raw tokens: we’re exposing additional fields in the usage API/SDKs and updating FAQ language. This is transparency / dispute reduction; not intended to change runtime behavior.
- Cache-hit attribution: no behavioral change expected from customers. It’s internal attribution + better reporting (and helps us explain why some requests are cheaper on our side). We’re not introducing a new customer-facing “cache discount” in the current quarter.

> B) For pricing experiment analysis: can we treat meter v2 as “measurement correction only,” or do we expect downstream changes?

Treat as measurement correction *but* analyses need explicit pre/post segmentation.
- We have at least two known confounders during the rollout window:
  1) Usage API field changes may reduce support-driven credits/disputes (affects net revenue, not usage).
  2) Some customers may re-run exports once fields are available; this can change reported numbers in customer spreadsheets but not actual consumption.
- For experiments, we’re tagging cohorts consistently now; however, any experiment readouts spanning the meter cutover should include a caveat slide + sensitivity check using both old vs new meter where possible (shadow compare).

> C) Any planned changes to free tier/overage copy, quotas, or plan limits that could change demand?

Not planning to change limits in late Feb.
- We do expect to finalize copy (language only) around billed tokens and retries; no product gating/price changes bundled with the meter fix.
- The only near-term risk: if we tighten idempotency expectations in SDK docs, a subset of customers might adjust retry logic, but again that should not meaningfully change usage volume.

One nuance for your model: embeddings batch fix could reduce billed units materially for a small number of heavy batchers. I’d recommend explicitly modeling that as a distribution (a few accounts) vs a uniform rate.

Happy to jump on a 15 min if you want to walk through the assumptions tab.

Nikhil

—
Nikhil Sharma
Director of Product, Hosted API
Redwood Inference

Laura — FYI, heard back from Nikhil (below). Net: treat meter v2 as measurement correction; minimal expectation of customer behavior change. They flagged that embeddings batch fix is concentrated in a few accounts (we’ll model as a tail rather than a blended rate).

Next steps on FP&A side:
1) Update GM model with “embeddings tail” scenario (top 10 batched-embeddings accounts sensitivity).
2) Add explicit pre/post segmentation note for experiment readouts and margin trend charts.
3) Add a line item in the forecast deck that separates: (a) meter correction impact, (b) credits/dispute reduction, (c) actual usage growth.

If you’re OK with these assumptions, we’ll treat this as the finance baseline for the Feb close and Q1 outlook.

Rishi
